dossier.public_summary: The 2.02-day dip lands on this fast-rotating M dwarf and its depth changes threefold between sectors. It matches the star's own 2.03-day spot rotation period and shows a phase-curve swing almost as large as the dip, both classic marks of stellar variability. Centroid and shape argue against a neighbour binary, but the variability is the best explanation.

reasons.why: Dip period is essentially identical to measured spot period in every sector with huge phase-curve swings. Coincidental alignment at 1x for a star varying at 2% depth is expected for rotation alias; with this amplitude and period equality variability is the best explanation, not a coincident planet.
reasons.value: rotation_d=2.029, signal_period_d=2.02183, signal_over_rotation=0.9964662395268605 (1x multiple), sector amplitudes 28103/46147/32050 ppm FA 2.908e-118/0.0/1.84e-171

reasons.why: Very large amplitude at the dip period, comparable to transit depth (rp=2.915 Rearth, undiluted 4789 ppm). Typical for spots, not an occultation; secondary snr=2.317 and odd_even diff_sigma=0.3069 have no binary sign but do not rule out stellar variability.
Depth strongly sector-dependent when it should be stable for a planet, consistent with changing spot coverage/aperture rather than a transit of a fixed object.
reasons.value: depths 2012 ppm (err 584), 6044 ppm (err 616), 4284 ppm (err 789) ppm p_constant=0.00001153 depth_change_pct=98.02; sector_depths_by_source verdict=changes_within_a_source within TESS-SPOC

reasons.why: Transit is much longer/borderline grazing for a TIC radius 0.3862 Rsun (and 1.37 Rsun with FLAME/GSP-Phot), favoring systematic shaping by variability over a planetary transit.
On-target locates dip to this rapidly rotating star itself, eliminating a neighbour eclipse but not an on-target stellar variability signal. xgboost planet_rank=0.11 supports this.
